title: Interface to Windows Named Pipes
text: {winpipe} exposes Win32 Named Pipes R connections read write . Named Pipes device inter-process communication (IPC) part file system allow fine-grained access control. R native support FIFOs Unix-like systems expose API named pipes Windows. Features: Create serve Windows named pipes, .e., R can client server Named pipes represented native R connections, .e., /O works box Let R talk non-R processes Can accept clients without blocking R session Includes interface SDDL

Another call read.csv() result error. can peek payload without consuming using np_peek(). confirms payload consumed giving number bytes left read. One cool thing named pipes access control. code: library(winpipe)  server <- winpipe("a-pipe") client <- winpipe("a-pipe", server = FALSE) write.csv(iris, file = client) head(read.csv(server)) #>   X Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species #> 1 1          5.1         3.5          1.4         0.2  setosa #> 2 2          4.9         3.0          1.4         0.2  setosa #> 3 3          4.7         3.2          1.3         0.2  setosa #> 4 4          4.6         3.1          1.5         0.2  setosa #> 5 5          5.0         3.6          1.4         0.2  setosa #> 6 6          5.4         3.9          1.7         0.4  setosa np_peek(server) #> [1] 0 sd <- sd_create(   ace(type = "deny", rights = "generic all", account = "everyone"),   ace(type = "allow", rights = "generic all", account = "admins"),   ace(type = "allow", rights = "generic all", account = "local system") ) sd #> <winpipe_sd> #> D:(D;;GA;;;WD)(A;;GA;;;BA)(A;;GA;;;SY) pipe <- winpipe("sd-pipe", sddl = sd) np_sd(pipe) #> <winpipe_sd> #> O:S-1-5-21-1492369709-893483088-3947136618-1001G:S-1-5-21-1492369709-893483088-3947136618-1001D:(D;;FA;;;WD)(A;;FA;;;BA)(A;;FA;;;SY)

what: Low-level information about a named pipe — np_config
title: Low-level information about a named pipe — np_config
text: Functions retrieve low-level information named pipe. np_config() returns pipe configuration. np_state() returns current clients. np_peek() looks bytes pipe without reading. np_sd() returns security descriptor.

title: Low-level information about a named pipe — np_config
Low-level information about a named pipe — np_config
text: con [winpipe]. open winpipe created winpipe.

title: Low-level information about a named pipe — np_config
text: np_config() returns: is_server is_client: Whether pipe started server client. is_message_type is_byte_type: Whether pipe reads data bytes messages. Pipes created using winpipe always read bytes. out_buffer_size in_buffer_size: Size input output chunks. max_instances: Maximum allowed instances. np_state() returns: state: reading mode pipe. Can either blocking non-blocking byte-mode message-mode. Pipes created using winpipe always blocking byte-mode. current_instances: Number instances related pipe. username: con server, reports username current client, . con client, NA. np_peek() returns number bytes available read pipe. np_peek() read pipe, returns error code warning. np_sd() returns object class winpipe_sd.

title: Low-level information about a named pipe — np_config
code: srv <- winpipe("test") cli <- winpipe("test")  np_config(srv) #> $is_server #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $is_client #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $is_message_type #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $is_byte_type #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $out_buffer_size #> [1] 1048576 #>  #> $in_buffer_size #> [1] 1048576 #>  #> $max_instances #> [1] 255 #>  np_state(srv) #> $state #> [1] "blocking byte-mode" #>  #> $current_instances #> [1] 1 #>  #> $username #> [1] "runneradmin" #>   np_peek(cli) #> [1] 0 writeLines("hello\nworld", cli) np_peek(cli) #> [1] 0 readLines(srv, n = 1) #> [1] "hello" np_peek(cli) #> [1] 0  close(srv) close(cli)

title: Security token information — np_whoami
text: Query Windows access token associated named pipe client calling R process. np_whoami() returns information token's user. np_token_info() returns full token details.

title: Security token information — np_whoami
text: con [winpipe] NULL. server end connected pipe, query connected client's token, NULL (default) query token R process .

title: Security token information — np_whoami
text: np_whoami() returns string form "DOMAIN\user". np_token_info() returns list : user: user name "DOMAIN\user". sid: user SID string. groups: data frame group names, SIDs, whether group enabled. elevated: whether token elevated (UAC). integrity: integrity level ("low", "medium", "high", "system"). token_type: "primary" (process) "impersonation" (pipe client). impersonation_level: impersonation tokens, one "anonymous", "identification", "impersonation", "delegation"; NA primary tokens.

title: Security token information — np_whoami
code: # If no argument is provided, returns the SID # of the R session np_whoami() #> [1] "runnervmdaln5\\runneradmin"  # If a server-client structure is provided # returns the SID of the client server <- winpipe("test") client <- winpipe("test") np_whoami(server) #> [1] "S-1-5-21-3776380004-1005456608-3524014338-500"  close(client) close(server)

title: Proxies — np_proxy
text: Starts local relay proxy named pipe. relay proxy lives background process r_bg. Essentially, way communicate named pipes HTTP requests. relay server takes HTTP requests client (e.g. curl httr2), sends named pipe using winpipe sends response back HTTP client. np_relay() workhorse function, contains server socket logic. np_proxy() simple wrapper starts relay server background process order block main session.

title: Proxies — np_proxy
code: np_proxy(name, port = httpuv::randomPort(), relay = np_relay)  np_relay(name, port)

title: Proxies — np_proxy
text: name [character(1)] Pipe name, without \\.\pipe\ prefix. port [numeric(1)] TCP port relay server listen . relay [function] relay function takes named pipe name port forwards requests responses server client. Defaults np_relay.

title: Proxies — np_proxy
text: np_proxy() returns object class winpipe_proxy. object contains base URL accepts requests process object manages server child process. np_relay() returns nothing runs server accepts requests long function running.

title: Proxies — np_proxy
code: # np_proxy() is a good way to communicate with named pipes # that communicate over HTTP, e.g., docker if (np_exists("docker_engine") && requireNamespace("httr2")) { library(httr2)  proxy <- np_proxy("docker_engine") on.exit(proxy$proc$kill())  # GET requests, e.g., to query the docker version resp <- request(proxy$base_url) %>%   req_url_path("/version") %>%   req_perform() %>%   resp_body_json() resp[c("Version", "ApiVersion", "Os")]  # POST requests, e.g., to create a container # do not run this if you don't wish to modify your docker state if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # pull image pull <- request(proxy$base_url) %>%   req_url_path("/images/create") %>%   req_url_query(fromImage = "hello-world", tag = "latest") %>%   req_method("POST") %>%   req_perform() pull$status_code  # create container created <- request(proxy$base_url) %>%   req_url_path("/containers/create") %>%   req_url_query(name = "winpipe-test") %>%   req_body_json(list(Image = "hello-world:latest")) %>%   req_perform() created$status_code } # } }

what: Build, parse and inspect security descriptors — security_descriptor
title: Build, parse and inspect security descriptors — security_descriptor
text: Security descriptors specify can read write Windows object named pipe. can passed winpipe(). security descriptor owner, primary group, DACL (may access pipe) SACL (auditing integrity labels). functions let construct convert SDDL string. sd_new() creates security descriptor. sd_add() appends one ace()s DACL SACL, creating ACL. sd_build() turns descriptor SDDL string. sd_parse() turns SDDL string descriptor. sd_default() returns default DACL current token.

title: Build, parse and inspect security descriptors — security_descriptor
code: sd_create(..., owner = NULL, group = NULL, dacl = NULL, sacl = NULL)  sd_add(sd, ..., acl = c("dacl", "sacl"))  sd_build(sd)  sd_parse(sddl)  sd_default()

title: Build, parse and inspect security descriptors — security_descriptor
text: ... One ace() objects. owner, group [character(1)] Owner primary group, alias, description SID. NULL, specify owner group. dacl, sacl [list] Optional ACL, list flags aces. sd [winpipe_sd] security descriptor created sd_create(). acl [character(1)] Type ACL add security descriptor. Can "dacl" "sacl". sddl [character(1)] SDDL string.

title: Build, parse and inspect security descriptors — security_descriptor
text: sd_new(), sd_add(), sd_parse() return "winpipe_sd" list. sd_build() sd_default() return

title: Build, parse and inspect security descriptors — security_descriptor
text: parsed descriptor list elements owner, group, dacl, sacl. Written string, descriptor looks like : prefix specifies owner, primary group DACL. Wrapped inside brackets individual aces, specify DACL configurations. Multiple ACEs can follow . ACE list type, flags, rights, object_guid, inherit, account extra. NULL DACL means section absent, whereas empty one (flags aces empty) grants nobody access.

title: Build, parse and inspect security descriptors — security_descriptor
code: x <- sd_create(owner = "admins") |>   sd_add(ace(rights = "generic all", account = "local system")) |>   sd_add(ace(rights = c("GR", "GW"), account = "authenticated users")) x #> <winpipe_sd> #> O:BAD:(A;;GA;;;SY)(A;;GRGW;;;AU) sd_build(x) #> [1] "O:BAD:(A;;GA;;;SY)(A;;GRGW;;;AU)"  identical(sd_parse(sd_build(sd_default())), sd_default()) #> [1] TRUE

what: winpipe: Interface to Windows Named Pipes — winpipe-package
title: winpipe: Interface to Windows Named Pipes — winpipe-package
text: Provides support Windows Named Pipes inter-process communication 'Win32' C++ API. Allows create, connect, disconnect, read , write server client pipes standard R connections. Includes convenience utilities parse build Access Control List (ACL) security descriptors. HTTP requests indirectly supported via background relay servers.

title: winpipe: Interface to Windows Named Pipes — winpipe-package
text: Maintainer: Jonas Lieth jonas.lieth@gesis.org [copyright holder]

title: Named pipes — winpipe
text: Functions create, open, close named pipes Windows. winpipe() creates new named pipe Windows. is_winpipe() checks object winpipe. np_listen() blocks session listens pipe. np_disconnect() disconnects client. np_exists() checks named pipe name exists. np_list() lists named pipes currently machine.

title: Named pipes — winpipe
code: winpipe(   name,   open = "r+",   server = !np_exists(name),   blocking = FALSE,   sddl = sd_default(),   max_instances = Inf,   timeout = getOption("timeout") )  # S3 method for class 'winpipe' open(con, open = "r+", blocking = FALSE, ...)  is_winpipe(x)  np_listen(con)  np_disconnect(con)  np_exists(name)  np_list()

title: Named pipes — winpipe
text: name [character(1)] Pipe name, without \\.\pipe\ prefix. open [character(1)] description open connection. See pipe. server [logical(1)] Whether connection opened server client. TRUE, creates pipe. FALSE, connects . Defaults TRUE pipe can found, otherwise FALSE. blocking [logical(1)] Whether connection blocking. See open. server, blocking open waits client connects (see timeout). non-blocking open returns immediately np_listen() can accept client later. reads, blocking connection waits data, non-blocking one returns available (possibly nothing) leaves partial line next read. Writes always block. Defaults FALSE. sddl [winpipe_sd] [character(1)] Security descriptor string, security descriptor built sd_create. Ignored server FALSE. Defaults default DACL current token (sd_default). max_instances [numeric(1)] Maximum allowed instances can opened named pipe. Can number 1 254. Inf, maximum 255 instances allowed. max_instances set creation pipe. means connections connecting existing pipe change maximum number instances. Defaults Inf. timeout [numeric(1)] Seconds without progress read, write, accept, open fails error. Inf, waits forever. Defaults getOption("timeout"). read times receiving bytes returns warning instead discarding . con [winpipe] winpipe connection created winpipe. ... arguments passed open. x object.

title: Named pipes — winpipe
text: Named pipes behave differently depending whether initialized server client. server = TRUE, open() creates named pipe client can connect . blocking = TRUE open waits client connect; otherwise run np_listen() block session one . np_disconnect() drops current client discards unread data. close() destroys instance disconnect first, data already written stays readable client. server = FALSE, named pipe created destroyed. Clients can read write change state named pipe. client named pipe opened server instance available answer , block session timeout reached interrupt signaled.
